title: What the vanishing $S(1) = 0$ means for the $c_k$ ladder
html:
This remark records what the classical vanishing S(1) = 0 implies for the c_k ladder, and the values at q_0 that go with it.

One reading has c_k coming from the u_{\text{ladder}} Taylor expansion of S(q) = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q)/E_0(q). Taken literally, this is degenerate. The Taylor expansion of S/S(1) around q = 1 is 0/0. The proved c_2 = -1 cannot be recovered this way.

The term S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / E_0 is the SDP-constraint scalar (canonical at q_0, matching the affine target n_{\text{target}} = S(q_0) \approx 0.18689). The c_k ladder normalization is \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / [Q_A \cdot \cos(\alpha_{\text{eff}})], with Q_A and \alpha read from the operator-valued N{=}3 witness. This proposition exposes the algebraic obstruction that identifies the missing categorical input (Q_A(q) and \alpha(q)).

The vanishing S(1) = 0 provides the direct-algebraic witness. An operator-theoretic witness arrives from the SDP strict-complementarity analysis. Both routes converge on the bare substrate scale Q_A. That scale is the retired Form A (+0.168\% without CODATA input, kept as a historical cross-check); the canonical \Delta base, evaluated with the Markov trace at z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1), gives 0.4491 MeV (-42.59\%) with the tower-summed E_0, or 0.4447 MeV with the order-zero one. The scored value is not the \Delta trace. It applies the T^3 weight split of the same z = q_0^3/(q_0^2+1) trace to the \gamma\gamma base V^3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 and gives \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.3254 MeV (-58.40\%) (Symbolic Q-value of free neutron decay). The \Delta value is kept as an unscored comparison. The correction to the base is the c_k ladder, which at z = q^3/(q^2+1) is not yet derived. Its normalization is not S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta/E_0.
